summary: The listing calendar write commands carry their JSON body shape, value types and live-change caution in --help, and `which` resolves write queries to them (plural and singular forms such as price/prices stem to the same key) without ranking them for read queries.
reason: The spec types these array bodies only as a bare label, so an agent could not build a valid --prices/--restrictions/--inventories value from the CLI alone, and the curated `which` index only knew read-side novel commands, so write queries returned unrelated ops commands. A dogfood resync rewrites the curated index from novel features and drops these entries, so a regen must re-add them.
validated_outcome: TestWhichRanksCalendarWritesFirst and TestWhichReadQueriesDoNotRankWrites pass on the 4.33.0 scorer; the write commands print their body shape and live-change caution in --help. TestWhichSingularStemsPluralsConsistently and TestWhichSingularFormsFindPriceCommands cover price/prices, rules and changes; `which "check listing price drift"` ranks price-parity and no write command.
